lesson_title: The Journey to Choose Our Leaders: Elections in India!

scenes.purpose: Introduce the lesson on elections in India.
scenes.teacher_script: Namaste, young citizens! Today, we're going on an exciting journey to understand how we choose our leaders in India through elections.

template_data.title: The Journey to Choose Our Leaders
template_data.subtitle: Understanding Elections in India

scenes.purpose: Explain the basic purpose and frequency of state assembly elections.
scenes.teacher_script: Every five years, people in our states get a chance to pick their representatives, called MLAs, for the State Legislative Assembly.

scenes.purpose: Outline the eligibility criteria for individuals to contest elections.
scenes.teacher_script: Not everyone can contest elections. There are important rules about who can stand as a candidate to become an MLA.

right_col.header: To Contest, a Person MUST NOT:
bullets: Hold any 'office of profit' under State/Central Govt.
Lack other qualifications prescribed by law

scenes.purpose: Differentiate between candidates fielded by political parties and independent candidates.
scenes.teacher_script: Candidates usually belong to political parties, but some individuals choose to contest on their own, known as Independents.

bullets: Political parties play a major role
Do not belong to any political party
Contest on their own (no party affiliation)

scenes.purpose: Explain how candidates and parties communicate their plans to voters.
scenes.teacher_script: Before elections, candidates and parties work hard to tell voters about their plans and promises through manifestos and campaigns.

attributes.name: Election Manifestos
attributes.value: Descriptions of programmes & promises relevant to local context

attributes.name: Campaigns
attributes.value: Candidates & supporters hold meetings, visit voters door-to-door

scenes.purpose: Define constituencies and explain the role of registered voters.
scenes.teacher_script: For elections, an area is divided into constituencies, and all registered voters in one constituency choose their MLA.

attributes.name: Constituency
attributes.value: An area (villages, towns, cities) from which one MLA is elected. Number varies by population (e.g., Hyderabad has 13).

attributes.name: Voters' Role
attributes.value: Get their names registered as voters in their area and vote to elect one member for the Assembly.

scenes.purpose: Illustrate the regular cycle of the election process.
scenes.teacher_script: The whole process of elections, from campaigning to voting and choosing MLAs, repeats in a regular cycle every five years.

template_data.title: The 5-Year Election Cycle
stages: Voters cast their votes in constituencies
MLAs are elected for five years

scenes.purpose: Assess the student's understanding of candidate qualifications.
scenes.teacher_script: Time for a quick check! Can you recall two main qualifications a person needs to contest elections in India?

template_data.question: What are two key qualifications required for a person to contest elections in India?
options: Must be 18 years old and wealthy
Must be a citizen of India and 25 years old
Must have a college degree and own property
Must be a local resident and know all voters
template_data.correct_answer: Must be a citizen of India and 25 years old
template_data.explanation: The textbook states a person must be a citizen of India and completed twenty-five years of age to contest elections.
